doc.title: Bob Haggart interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995

title: Big Noise revivals and royalties
summary: Lead sheets for a women's band, a Hardee's commercial and Linda Ronstadt's What's New brought royalties.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Did it ever get, finally get written down?

Well I’ve written it out for people, yeah. In fact there’s a guy that contacted me, wanted to make an arrangement for his, he had a girl band. And I forget the name of his band but it’s a new group. They were all women. And they have a terrific bass player and they do “Big Noise,” but they don’t do it like I did it. They have their own way of doing it and it’s a lot of stuff, and it starts off with the sticks on the bass, and then there’s sticks on the guitar, and then on the tom tom. It’s all percussive, the whole thing. And it’s terrific. He sent me the tape of this thing. But he said would I send him a lead sheet of just the way I did it so I sent him a lead sheet. There’s a regular melody to it, you know [humms]. It goes on and on and different parts to it. So she said that the girl bass player’s going to make an arrangement for the whole band and it’s very, supposed to be very exciting and everything, you know a lot of high trumpets. I’m anxious to hear it. So that’s—that thing just stays alive, getting people. You keep hearing it in commercials. It was just in a
Hardee’s commercial, you know the Hardee’s Restaurant chain? And so I got a nice fat check for that.
Doesn’t it feel good to finally get some royalties?
Finally get some of your due there.

Well, like Linda Rondstadt’s record of “What’s New.” That was a pretty nice, talking about money. It sold over 2 million. I’m one of the writers of “What’s New.” So that came in handy, too. Sounds like I’m bragging, doesn’t it?
